source.title: Realistic shell-model calculations: current status and open problems

accepted.question_text: How should realistic shell-model effective interactions for medium- and heavy-mass nuclei be extended to include the contribution of three-body forces, given that most current shell-model calculations derive the effective interaction from two-body low-momentum nucleon-nucleon interactions alone even though calculations for systems with more than two nucleons depend on omitted induced and genuine many-body components?
accepted.context_brief: Three-body forces in shell-model effective interactions

evidence.quote: It is certainly a major open problem to investigate the contribution of three-body forces to the shell-model effective interaction.

Note that the inclusion of forces beyond the two-body ones has been essentially limited to few-nucleon systems. As regards medium- and heavy-mass nuclei, only the NN potential is used at present in the derivation of the shell-model effective interaction.

accepted.question_text: For low-momentum shell-model effective interactions derived from phase-shift equivalent nucleon-nucleon potentials, how sensitive are the resulting shell-model observables to moderate variations of the cutoff momentum Λ, and how should that cutoff dependence be characterized or controlled?

evidence.quote: We have found [25], however, that the shell-model results do not change significantly for moderate variations of the cutoff around this value.
Further study is certainly needed to better clarify the effect of cutoff variations on shell-model effective interactions.

accepted.question_text: How can one establish the convergence properties of the Qˆ-box expansion used to derive shell-model effective interactions, especially the size and necessity of contributions beyond second order and the extent to which folded-diagram summations compensate higher-order Qˆ-box terms?

evidence.quote: The convergence of the Qˆ-box, however, still remains to some extent an open problem, although it has been shown that the differences in Veff’s calculated with Qˆ-boxes to various orders, are attenuated when the folded diagrams are summed to all orders [30].
However, the final conclusion of [30] was that third-order calculations should be employed since third-order terms of the Qˆ-box are not negligible.

accepted.question_text: When the auxiliary one-body potential U in realistic shell-model calculations is taken to be a harmonic-oscillator potential rather than a Hartree-Fock self-consistent potential, is it justified to omit diagrams containing U and bubble insertions on the assumption that they cancel, or do those omitted terms make a significant contribution to the effective interaction?
accepted.context_brief: Validity of omitting U and bubble diagrams

evidence.quote: However, in almost all calculations performed so far diagrams with the U potential and bubble insertions are not included. This assumption is based on the fact that these diagrams would cancel each other when using for U the Hartree-Fock self-consistent potential.
The most common choice, however, is the harmonic oscillator potential, and the plausibility of the above approximation remains to be ascertained.

accepted.question_text: As the number of valence nucleons increases away from a doubly magic core, why do realistic shell-model calculations increasingly overestimate ground-state energies in long isotopic or isotonic chains, and to what extent is that overbinding caused by missing many-body forces, especially three-body forces, versus missing higher-order contributions such as third-order Qˆ-box diagrams?

evidence.quote: It is, of course, a very interesting problem to find out what happens with increasing number of valence nucleons.
However, the ground-state energy, which is well reproduced for the two-valence-proton nucleus 134Te, is increasingly overestimated with increasing number of protons.
In summary, we may say that a deeper comprehension of the role of both genuine and effective three-body forces and of contributions to the Qˆ-box beyond second order certainly deserves further study.

accepted.question_text: Why is the agreement between theory and experiment generally worse for nuclei in which hole-hole interaction matrix elements are relevant than for nuclei dominated by particle-particle or particle-hole matrix elements, and what physical or methodological origin explains this asymmetry?

evidence.quote: While the overall agreement between theory and experiment may be considered satisfactory in most cases, it is not in general of the same quality as that obtained for nuclei in which there is no hole-hole interaction.
At present, we don’t have a clear understanding of the origin of this dissimetry.

accepted.question_text: How should realistic shell-model calculations incorporate coupling to the scattering continuum for nuclei near the drip lines, where continuum effects are expected to play an important role in the structure and spectroscopy of weakly bound systems?

evidence.quote: This is certainly the case of the coupling with the scattering continuum which should play an important role in nuclei near the drip lines.
We hope, however, to have succeeded in highlighting the value of realistic shell-model calculations and the need for further efforts to clarify some remaining open questions.
